title: Field-Level Diff — Core Method
description: Database descriptions lie by omission, so the inspector diffs records field by field: for any two records it lists added, removed, and changed fields with old and new values. Diffs ignore volatile fields like last-seen timestamps when configured to, keeping the signal clean. This is the tool you reach for when a record 'changed but nothing changed' — the diff shows exactly what moved. Field-level comparison is the ground truth beneath every schema summary. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
provenance: JAH Databases archive-intelligence tools program, lane T2a — public methods from established computer-science practice.

title: Per-Record Anomaly Flags — Core Method
description: Instead of trusting aggregates, the inspector scores each record against the population: values far from the field's typical range, types that disagree with the schema, strings where numbers are expected. Flags are attached to the record with the rule that fired and the observed deviation, so a human can judge. A record can carry several flags, and flag patterns across records reveal systematic ingestion bugs. This is data quality work at the finest grain — one record at a time. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Null Audit — Core Method
description: Missing data hides in many costumes: null, empty string, 'N/A', zero, epoch zero. The null auditor checks every field of a record against the full costume list and reports which fields are effectively empty. Per-record null maps roll up into per-field null rates, which is how you discover that 'optional' field nobody ever fills. Distinguishing 'missing' from 'empty' from 'zero' matters, because each means something different downstream. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Value Distributions — Core Method
description: One record means little without the population behind it: the inspector shows each field's value in the context of its distribution — percentiles for numbers, top values for categories. A value at the 99.9th percentile deserves a second look; a category value never seen before deserves a third. Distributions are computed on samples for large tables and cached per field. Context turns raw values into judgments. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.

title: Lineage Tracing — Core Method
description: Every record came from somewhere: the inspector traces a record's lineage through ingestion logs, transformation steps, and source identifiers back to its origin. Each hop records what changed — normalized, merged, re-encoded — so the current bytes are fully explainable. Broken lineage, where a hop is missing, is flagged rather than hidden. When a record looks wrong, lineage tells you whether the source was wrong or the pipeline was. At ladder rank 1 this is the simple core: a single, self-contained application of the method.
